title: Anti-fascist march held in Patras following attack on students

tea.why: Protesters marched to condemn a violent attack by a group of individuals against students and supporters in the Neapoli Zarouchleika area.
tea.want: Participants demanded the identification and arrest of the perpetrators and an end to the prosecution of the victims of the attack.
tea.changed: Nov 5: Authorities reported 12 arrests and the seizure of a firearm and other items from a vehicle following the incident.

summary: On November 4, 2026, a large anti-fascist march took place in Patras, Greece, starting from Tarampoura Square. The protest was organized by the Patras Labour Centre, the municipal authority, student unions, and various workers' organizations to condemn a violent attack that occurred on the night of November 3. Reports state that a group of approximately 40 individuals attacked students and supporters, resulting in eight injuries. The demonstrators marched through the city to express opposition to fascist practices. The Mayor of Patras and representatives from the Communist Party of Greece (KKE) participated in the event. Authorities have since arrested 12 individuals in connection with the incident, and investigations are ongoing regarding charges of assault and weapons violations.
demands: Stop the prosecution of the victims
response: Police arrested 12 individuals, including one minor. During investigations, officers seized a firearm, a replica knuckle duster, a full-face mask, a helmet, and cannabis from a vehicle. Charges include assault and weapons violations.

updates.text: A group of individuals attacked students and supporters in the Neapoli Zarouchleika area, resulting in eight injuries.
A protest march took place in Patras to condemn the attack.
Police announced 12 arrests and the seizure of weapons and other items related to the investigation.
